summary: SunZia Transmission, LLC files limited tariff revisions under section 205 on November 16, 2026, in ER27-515-000. SunZia serves no load, so it amends Section 8 of its transmission owner tariff to say the CAISO tariff controls interconnection of generation and co-located load, and it reserves the right to amend once it sees the other owners' filings.
ask: Accept the revisions effective 60 days after FERC's order, and find them consistent with the show cause order.

points.point: The line is a 552-mile high voltage direct current line in New Mexico and Arizona.
points.quote: an approximately 552-mile, bi-pole, high voltage direct current (“HVDC”) 500 kV transmission line

points.point: All of the line's capacity is committed to two wind subscribers.
points.quote: the entire capacity of the Transmission System is committed to two Subscribers

points.point: Its tariff is silent on load interconnection because it does not serve load, so it says no large load provisions are needed.
points.quote: SunZia Transmission does not directly serve load and, accordingly, there are no provisions in its TO Tariff that address the interconnection of the load to the SunZia Transmission System

points.point: Interconnection requests already go to CAISO first.
points.quote: Section 8 of the SunZia Transmission TO Tariff states that all requests for interconnection to the SunZia Transmission System must be directed in the first instance to CAISO

points.point: The only edit confirms the CAISO tariff controls generator and co-located interconnection.
points.quote: Section 8 of the TO Tariff has been amended to clarify that the CAISO Tariff will continue to control with respect to the interconnection of Generating Units

points.point: SunZia keeps the option to amend after reviewing the other owners' filings.
points.quote: reserves the right, following review of the proposed tariff changes filed by the other Participating Transmission Owners

points.point: SunZia wants CAISO to start its electrically proximate load work as soon as possible.
points.quote: SunZia Transmission continues to support the need to apply these enhanced Large Load interconnection procedures to Electrically Proximate Loads

points.point: The effective date is tied to FERC's order. The tariff records carry a placeholder date until then.
points.quote: SunZia Transmission proposes an effective date of sixty days after the Commission issues an order on this compliance filing for the changes to its TO Tariff

throughLine.text: Filed under section 205 to answer the E-10 show cause order. It adds no large load study process, cost recovery agreement or flexible service, and says the CAISO tariff is where those changes belong.

figures.label: Line transmission capacity
figures.quote: with a transmission capacity of 3,021 MW in New Mexico and Arizona
